restrictions: Messages are exactly 135 bytes, so the single padded block ends in 0x86; c+p = 520 initial-state bits are fixed.
Uses the complete fixed-zero-state SHA3-256 sponge with 0x06 suffix padding and prefix rounds 0 through 4, as in verifier/keccak.py:sha3_256(data, 5).

Differential construction of Guo-Liao-Liu-Liu-Qiao-Song (JoC 2020, ePrint 2019/147): 2-round linearized connector for rounds 0-1 and trail core No. 3 for rounds 2-4, adapted from their 1084-bit inputs (p = 4) to byte-aligned inputs (p = 8).
The published 1084-bit colliding pair is verified with the organizer permutation as evidence only; it is outside the byte-string domain and is not used as a certificate or by the algorithm.

Connector cost is charged from the paper's measured 428.8 single-core hours per successful space with an 8x per-space budget, 128 spaces and a ceiling of 2^48 RAM primitives per core-hour; trail-core search is charged as preprocessing.
Heuristic, exploratory claim: no byte-aligned collision has been produced; the score depends on declared heuristics H1-H4.
The nominal reference identifier does not itself assert an improvement.

heuristics.statement: For trail core No. 3 and byte-aligned 135-byte messages (p = 8 fixed padding bits instead of the paper's p = 4), the GLL+20 2-round connector, run with fresh random beta1, beta0-subset and linearization choices, succeeds with expected cost at most 2 x 428.8 single-core hours of the authors' implementation per successful space, and each successful space has dimension DF >= 33.
heuristics.scope: Single-block 5-round SHA3-256 from the all-zero state; 2-round connector for rounds 0-1 targeting alpha2 = L^-1(beta2) of trail core No. 3; 520 fixed initial-state bits.
heuristics.extrapolation: Extrapolates the one reported p = 4 connector run (T_c = 428.8 core-hours, DF = 37) to p = 8 using GLL+20 Eq. 10 (DF falls by at most 4 when four fixed bits are added) and assumes the success rate of consistent linearizations drops by at most 2x. The 8x budget plus Markov's inequality converts the expectation into a fixed budget with failure probability at most 1/4.
heuristics.limitations: The connector has not been run by this submitter for p = 8. The 428.8 h figure is a single reported run, not a mean. More fixed bits could reduce consistent linearizations by more than 2x or make DF fall below 33; each 2x excess in cost adds 1 bit to the score. If DF were lower, more spaces (more connector runs) would be needed.

heuristics.statement: For message pairs (M, M + Delta) drawn from connector spaces, the probability of a full 256-bit digest collision is at least 2^-37.7 (the paper's multi-trail estimate 2^-36.70 halved), and the number of collisions among the 128 x 2^32 counted pairs is close enough to Poisson that Pr[no collision] <= exp(-2.46).
heuristics.scope: Rounds 2-4 of 5-round SHA3-256 after the connector, trail core No. 3 with all round-3/round-4 continuations that end in digest collisions.
heuristics.extrapolation: Extends the paper's single observation (one collision in one DF-37 space) and its weight estimate to 128 independently generated byte-aligned spaces; within a space the pairs are correlated.
heuristics.limitations: Supported by one published collision and a trail-weight estimate, not by sampled statistics. Clustering within a space could lower the success probability; the declared 0.5 is below the computed 0.66 for that reason. Each halving of the true probability adds about 1 bit.

heuristics.statement: One single-core CPU hour of the authors' connector implementation performs at most 2^48 primitive 256-bit-RAM operations (loads, stores, ALU, branches) of the v5 model, so it costs at most 2^48/1355 = 2^37.60 units.
heuristics.scope: Conversion of the paper's measured connector time T_c into v5 units.
heuristics.extrapolation: Assumes a clock frequency at most about 5 GHz and at most about 15.6 primitive-equivalent operations retired per cycle, which is above 4-wide retirement even when every micro-op is a 512-bit operation counted as two 256-bit primitives.
heuristics.limitations: The paper does not name the CPU. The conversion bounds instruction throughput, not the algorithm's intrinsic operation count. An unusually wide or fast core would invalidate the ceiling, but a realistic core is about 4x below it.

heuristics.statement: The GLL+20 Appendix C.2 trail search that yields core No. 3 costs at most 2^13 cores x (2^36 + 2^35) extensions x 2^14 primitives plus 2^62 primitives for KeccakTools core generation, at most 2^64.0 primitives (2^53.6 units), with at most 2^30 bytes of memory.
heuristics.scope: Preprocessing that recomputes the hard-coded trail core.
heuristics.extrapolation: The paper states thresholds (C1 <= 2^36, C2 <= 2^35) and 'more than 3000' cores rather than run times; the count is bounded at 2^13.
heuristics.limitations: No published run time for the search. This term changes the total by about 0.2 bits; even a 16x excess would add under 1.5 bits.
